title: Reversing a Priced Fill on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
A fill already priced on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan is corrected by reversing that exact fill and, where a correction is due, pricing a fresh fill in its place.

## The conditions on a reversal

1. The reversal names the single priced fill it applies to, and that fill is on record as paid or as adjusted.
2. No reversal of that same priced fill is already on record.

Both are settled on the pharmacy record before the reversal is made; each fill is reversed on its own reference, and a prescription with several refills is never reversed as a whole.

## What a reversal carries and what it undoes

The reversal carries the negative of what the member and the plan paid, so the out-of-pocket accumulator and the payment stage return to what they were before the fill.

## Who may have a fill reversed

| The circumstance | Whether the fill may be reversed |
| --- | --- |
| The pharmacy never handed the drug over | yes |
| The member returns an unopened product where state law lets them | yes |
| The member has taken the drug away, and says so on the telephone | no; a fill the member has taken away is never reversed on the member's word alone |

## Where a correction follows an approved exception

Where the correction follows an approved exception the fresh fill is priced at the tier the decision directs, and the difference is refunded to the member.

A refill is refused as too soon until the member has used the threshold percentage of the previous days supply written for the plan held.
